assumptions: The founder exports requests they already hold (feedback board, CRM lost reasons, support tags or a spreadsheet) as CSV with contact, date and request columns; at most 150 rows and 24000 characters.
Relationship labels come from the founder's export; rows without one are ranked as unknown, in the Tell group.
A match is only as good as the request text: vague requests are expected to land in no or check-by-hand, not in a group.
effects: Writes reports/CLOSE_THE_LOOP.md in the bound project.
Sends request text and the shipped description, never contacts or names, to the managed match and draft model routes.
Sends, publishes and changes nothing else.
cost_drivers: Rows and request length decide whether matching takes one or two calls on the match route.
The draft route is called once, and only when at least one person matched.

rubric.question: Is every person placed in a group someone whose quoted words, found verbatim in their request, actually ask for what shipped?
Do the drafts describe only what the shipped text says, with partial matches flagged for the founder before sending?
Could the founder start at the top of the list and send, without re-reading the whole export?

cases.description: Mixed export: a churned customer and a lost deal who asked, a lead who asked, a customer who asked twice, and unrelated requests.
